title.en: Zipper tapes, element rows and slider closure

summary: Build a readable zipper assembly whose slider, paired element rows and fabric attachment remain distinct in open and closed poses.
objective: Build a readable zipper assembly whose slider, paired element rows and fabric attachment remain distinct in open and closed poses.
intent_signals: Build a readable zipper assembly whose slider, paired element rows and fabric attachment remain distinct in open and closed poses.
example_prompts: Build an explorable zipper tapes, element rows and slider closure and expose its construction at close range.

principles: Choose a closed-end discrete-element teaching zipper; coil and separating zippers require different element/termination geometry. Tape, elements and slider have different roles and should not collapse into one metallic strip.
Define the assembly path and closure state before embroidery or scratches. A slider-shaped ornament alone does not establish a working closure.
implementation: Create two tapes with finite thickness, sewn attachment margins and element anchor edges. Add discrete complementary element shapes, a slider body with two entry channels merging into one exit, a separately hinged pull tab and authored end stops. Shape the channel and element engagement from a chosen reference rather than stamping identical intersecting cubes.

Use path coordinate s and a bounded slider position as authority. Derive paired/open element positions from the same closure boundary; preserve element IDs and count during opening. Place the closed chain behind the closing slider and separated tapes ahead, with an authored transition region inside its channel. This is a kinematic teaching layout, not deformable tooth contact.

Limit slider travel to the authored stops; animate pull-tab hinge angle independently without moving the closure boundary. Reset slider, element poses, tape spread and tab angle from the same snapshot.

At overview distance keep the two tape borders, chain line and pull aperture. In a closeup retain channel thickness, element interlock silhouette and stitch attachment; simplify thread fibers first. A bright pull and muted tape are optional style choices.
observable_checks: Scrub closed, halfway and open: each element stays attached to its own tape and the closure boundary follows the slider without creating or deleting teeth.
Inspect front, side and slider cutaway: element paths enter the intended channels and the pull hinge has a real pivot; no visible element floats across a channel wall in the authored travel range.
Reset from a partial closure and compare all part transforms and slider position with the saved initial state.

known_limits: No pull-force, jam, tooth-contact, fabric stress or waterproofness model. The teaching construction is not a manufacturing drawing.
Authored construction and prospective checks; no runtime artifact, render or material test has been executed for this record.
creative_affordances: Use toy-sized elements, a technical cutaway or a stylized travel-bag closure; keep the tape/element/slider roles even when surface detail is sparse.

claims.statement: YKK identifies tape, elements and slider as the three major parts of a zipper.
claims.scope: Part taxonomy only; the chosen closed-end geometry and kinematic transition are authored.
